summary: Source-review plan for USB 3 SuperSpeed Gen1 device mode from the bare-metal loader. It covers: (1) a 25-step ordered register sequence S0-S25 with physical addresses, values and pinned citations: GUSB3PIPECTL pre-setup, the GPC7_1 orientation read, PMU 0x12860620 isolation release, USBCON ready_to_pipe3, SNPS USB/DP combo-PHY reset/initiate/SRAM init, the 6144-word cp_int_ref_x2_code firmware load over the CR port, RX calibration, tuning, link de-emphasis, TCA NC->USB, core soft reset, the glue LLUCTL/FORCE_GEN1/LSKIPFREQ/GUCTL1 settings, DCFG=SS, U1/U2 off, and the SS protocol work in the engine. Every SS step is classed must-do; only the USB2 prerequisites are inherited. (2) The DWC3 behaviour when training fails: the vendor has no software fallback, the speed is taken from DSTS at CONNECTDONE, and reconnect needs a core soft reset. It gives a bounded polled fallback: P0 PHY deadlines, P1 T_SS about 1.5 s with an LTSSM trace, and FORCED = run_stop off + pipe3_disable + usbmon_init at HS, once per boot. (3) Twelve unknowns, each with a read-only check that uses no debugfs, and the four USB rails. (4) Effort/risk and a read-only native probe as the first experiment.
established: The compiled e1s SS path is phy-exynos-usbdrd-eusb.c + exynos-usb-blkcon.c + phy-exynos-snps-usbdp.c (CONFIG_PHY_EXYNOS_USBDRD_EUSB=m)
The DT selects sub_phy_version 0x801 (RAM code cp_int_ref_x2_code, skip_check_ack), RAM mode, force_gen1 and dis-u1/u2 quirks
Orientation is read from GPIO gpc7-1 (PERIC2 0x11830000 bank 0x1a0) because CONFIG_CHECK_CTYPE_SIDE is not set
The probe resource map: USBCON 0x178a0000, USBDP ctrl 0x178d0000, TCA 0x178e0000, link 0x17900000; pipe3 PMU isolation at 0x12860620 bit 0
The vendor driver has no software SS->HS fallback; reconnect requires a core soft reset (gadget.c:2657-2662)
Prior repository evidence: NAT-039 Android current_speed=high-speed with maximum_speed=super-speed; S-Boot upload mode enumerated at 480 Mbps
The SNPS PHY CAL bounded loops differ from the BSP tree f85e53cf, and the RAM code, register headers, blkcon, eusb glue and usb dtsi are byte-identical between the two trees
